dataset_description: Python files from public GitHub (BigQuery github_repos via transformersbook/codeparrot), exact-deduplicated and heuristically filtered by the CodeParrot authors. The dataset card declares no license of its own; each row carries the license of its source repository.
why_not_github_code_clean: codeparrot/github-code-clean is also ungated, but it mixes ~30 languages in 880 x ~355 MB parquet shards (Python ~6% of rows), so ~1 GB of permissive Python would need ~10 GB of download plus pyarrow. codeparrot-clean is Python-only with the same per-file license column.
rights_basis: Each file keeps repo_name, path and license so attribution/NOTICE obligations of MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD and ISC can be met. Per-file license is the repository-level license detected by GitHub/BigQuery, not a per-file audit.
redistribution: Internal research use. Before redistributing, re-check licenses and carry attribution (repo_name/path) per the original licenses.

decontamination_sources.use: blocklist only; no benchmark text is included in any output

processing.line_endings: CRLF and CR normalized to LF before all hashing and filtering

filters.utf8: strict encode; files containing U+FFFD or NUL dropped
filters.python3: must parse with ast.parse on CPython 3.10.9 (drops Python 2 sources)

dedupe.order: shard name, then row; first occurrence kept
dedupe.near: sha256 of content with '#' comment lines removed and all whitespace removed

decontamination.method: item-relative 10-token n-gram containment: drop a file when it contains >= 50% of any blocklist item's distinct n-grams (tokens = regex \w+|[^\w\s]); items shorter than 10 tokens matched as whitespace-free substrings

processing.docstring_pairs: ast FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef (incl. methods/nested) with a docstring >= 8 chars on its own lines and >= 1 statement after it; prompt = def line through docstring, completion = remaining body, both dedented to the def, and prompt+completion must re-parse; prompt <= 4096, completion <= 8192 chars; deduped by whitespace-free sha256 within split and val pairs also present in train dropped

limitations: GitHub snapshot (~2016-2022 BigQuery dump); repository-level license labels; heuristic autogen/minified detection; near-dedupe is hash-based (not MinHash), so lightly edited copies survive.
